title: Minimum Skips to Arrive at Meeting On Time
summary: Given the number of hours before a meeting, an array of road distances, and a travel speed, determine the minimum number of skips required to arrive at the meeting on time.
statement: Given the number of hours before a meeting, an array of road distances, and a travel speed, determine the minimum number of skips required to arrive at the meeting on time. If it is impossible to arrive on time, return -1. After traveling each road, you must wait until the next full hour before starting the next road, except after the last road. Skipping a rest allows you to start the next road immediately, potentially finishing at a non-integer hour.
constraints: speed and hours_before are positive integers.
After each non-final road, either wait until the next integer hour or spend one skip to depart immediately.
hints: Represent elapsed time in distance units so one hour equals speed units and all arithmetic stays exact.
For each road and skip count, either round up at the rest or use another skip and keep the exact elapsed value.
Do not round after the final road; then choose the smallest skip count within hours_before*speed.
The DP retains the least elapsed time for every prefix and skip count, and the two transitions cover every possible rest decision.
editorial: The DP retains the least elapsed time for every prefix and skip count, and the two transitions cover every possible rest decision.

tests.explanation: Skipping the wait after the first road permits arrival within two hours, so one skip is sufficient.
Even skipping every rest cannot reduce pure travel time below ten hours, so the answer is -1.
